'''Rachel M. Hilliam''' is a British statistician, a scholar of [[statistics education]],{{r|sig}} and a former [[medical statistician]]. She is a professor of statistics at the [[Open University]], where she heads the School of Mathematics and Statistics.{{r|ou}}

==Education and career==
Hilliam received a 2000 Ph.D. from [[De Montfort University]] for her dissertation ''Statistical discrimination with disease categories subject to misclassification''.{{r|diss}}

She joined the Open University in 2011,{{r|ou}} after previously serving as the medical statistician for Derby Hospitals Trust. She became the founding chair of the Alliance for Data Science Professionals, an accreditation organisation for [[data science]] founded jointly in 2022 by the [[Royal Statistical Society]], [[British Computer Society]], and [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]].{{r|cw}}

==Recognition==
Hilliam received the 2024 Chambers Medal of the [[Royal Statistical Society]], jointly with John MacInnes, for her outstanding service to the society.{{r|chambers}} She was the Teaching Statistics Trust Lecturer for 2025–2026.{{r|ou}} She was named as an officer of the [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2026 Birthday Honours]].{{r|obe}}
